script.title: The Case of the Overloaded Hook (Part 1 of 2)
script.synopsis: In blue-hour stillness the Inspector stakes out a sagging coat hook beside four empty ones, logging 'No movement' while jump cuts show the heap growing. In the last 4 s the camera drops inside the heap and sees her lay one more coat on top from her own forearm, eyes on the empty doorway; she does not react. Part 2 outline (same hallway, same single character, 28-30 s): she reviews the evidence from the low heap angle, counts the coats against the coat habit on her own forearm, and reconstructs the jump-cut gaps; the Part 2 verdict is where the signature two-finger clipboard tap is used for the first time, saved there on purpose and not used in Part 1. She says 'The culprit works quickly. The culprit is me.', hangs one coat on each empty hook, and turns with the last coat over her forearm to hang it back on the original hook.

beats.beat: Wide of four bare hooks and one buckling hook; 'No movement.'
Jump cut: heap chest-high, same line, same pose.
Jump cut: heap shoulder-high; she checks the doorway.
Jump cut: heap taller than her; beam steadier and prouder.
Low angle inside the heap: she lays one more coat on top from her own forearm, eyes on the doorway.
Freeze on the unreacting Inspector; tap saved for Part 2 verdict, which hangs the coats and exposes her.

dialogue.speaker: Inspector
dialogue.delivery: flat, measured, tick of pencil under the line

script.caption_text: Part 1 of 2. Nothing has moved. Nothing at all.

scenes.location: Hallway with coat hooks, early-morning blue hour
scenes.action: Locked-off wide: the Inspector stands square to the rail, chest lamp pinned on the bowed fifth hook under a waist-high coat heap. She lifts the clipboard, makes one flat pencil tick, and says her line while the rail creaks.
scenes.performance: Invested task: keep the lamp beam exactly on the sagging hook and log it; eyes fixed on the heap, never the lens, as if the hook might bolt.
scenes.microexpression: Neutral; one slow blink as the rail creaks.

scenes.lighting: Key: cool blue-hour daylight from the frosted door panel on frame-left, soft and low; fill: the Inspector's chest lamp as a bright circular pool on the heap; colour bounce: pale blue-grey from the plaster wall onto the left side of her jacket, aubergine reading nearly black; contact shadows: hard under the heap where it meets the floor and under each empty hook. continuity.identity_anchors: Aubergine utility jacket with four flap pockets, bright circular inspection lamp on a chest strap, tiny clipboard on a lanyard, hair in a tight low bun. Oval face, straight dark brows, small round glasses pushed slightly down the nose, neutral expression that breaks into warm disappointment rather than anger.
continuity.costume: Aubergine utility jacket with four flap pockets, chest-strap inspection lamp, tiny clipboard on a lanyard, tight low bun, small round glasses. Same costume in every scene; no brand marks.
continuity.notes: Props besides fixed costume: coat heap (1), grey-green coat on her left forearm (2); hook rail is set. Heap height per scene: waist, chest, shoulder, above head, then topped by the forearm coat. Moving props: coat heap grows between cuts; coat on forearm moves onto the heap in S5. Lighting is blue hour only: frosted door panel plus chest lamp, no room lights, no switches. The two-finger clipboard tap is NOT used in Part 1 and is saved for the Part 2 verdict. Speech maximum 3 words in 6 s, well under 2.8 words/s. No off-camera voice. Part 2 introduces no new characters or locations.

growth_hypotheses.hypothesis: A repeated identical frame with a visibly growing heap keeps muted viewers to the end because the unresolved final shot demands Part 2.
growth_hypotheses.metric: Average completion rate and Part 2 click-through
growth_hypotheses.falsifier: Completion below 50% or Part 2 views under 20% of Part 1 views

growth_hypotheses.hypothesis: The self-implicating last shot drives shares to a friend who piles coats.
growth_hypotheses.falsifier: Shares per 1,000 views not above the channel median
